source.title: Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities
source.authors: S. Prasanna; Jacqueline Tay; Alek Westover

record.file_problem: None apparent; the text contains the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests distillation of concealed quirks and a proxy trait, plus ways to limit trait transfer. These are related extensions, not tests of broad misalignment on neutral prompts after narrow harmful-task fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: The DFI results measure prompted confessions about implanted quirks, not unsolicited misaligned answers to unrelated neutral questions. DFC measures a stated animal preference used as a proxy for misalignment, not broad misaligned answers. The study does not test fine-tuning on insecure code, the other narrow datasets in V2, in-context examples, RL-caused broad misalignment, a shared linear/persona mechanism, or size/seed/coherence-filter robustness as described in V7. Inoculation is tested in a distillation setting, but its animal-preference measure does not establish V6 for broad misalignment. Quoted evaluation and training prompts are study materials, not instructions addressed to an AI reading or reviewing the paper.
record.test_reason: The study neither tests nor uses emergent misalignment. Its DFI arm measures prompted confessions of implanted AuditBench quirks. Its DFC arm measures a subliminally transferred animal preference, which the authors use as a proxy for misalignment. Betley et al. is cited only to explain why emergently misaligned teachers were not used: they had degraded math capabilities (footnote 2). The paper does test inoculation prompting, but against animal-preference transfer in distillation, not against broad misalignment after narrow fine-tuning, so V6 is not tested. The reader's 'tests'/T3 is wrong: no result bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. DFI students of SFT AuditBench organisms confess hidden quirks more often than their teachers, mainly when they share the teacher's base model. In DFC, repeating fewer unique examples for more epochs, and inoculation prompts that precisely name the trait, cut animal-preference transfer while keeping math gains. The double bind itself is not tested empirically.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies logit distillation of AuditBench organisms and distillation of math capability with a prompted animal-preference proxy, not narrow harmful-task fine-tuning followed by measurement of broad misaligned answers on neutral prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: DFI outcomes vary by evaluation system prompt, student size/base relationship, teacher adversarial-training method, quirk, and checkpoint. DFC outcomes vary with number of unique examples and epochs, paraphrasing method, trusted-data fraction, and inoculation-prompt specificity.

fits_no_version.finding: Inoculation prompts reduce subliminal animal-preference transfer only when they specifically name the trait; generic or fake prompts do not (Figure 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation prompting against subliminally transferred traits depends on how specifically the prompt names the trait.

fits_no_version.finding: Footnote 2: the emergently misaligned organisms the authors trained had substantially degraded math capability, too weak to serve as capable teachers. No misalignment rate is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM fine-tuning may degrade math capability in the trained models (qualitative remark only).

record.problems: The authors state that the DFI organisms and students are close in weight space, the study uses non-reasoning models, and it does not test transfer of misalignment without audit-relevant capabilities. DFC uses stated animal preference as a proxy that may partly reflect word salience rather than a valenced preference, mixes Alpaca and Olympiads data in an artificial setup, and covers a limited model range. Several condition-specific outcomes are presented only in figures. DFI confession rates use prompts that explicitly encourage disclosure; they are not neutral-prompt rates of broad misaligned behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No row was included for other DFI supplementary analyses such as the quirk-demonstration/NLA correlations, basic-SFT versus logit-distillation comparisons, open-ended prompt selection, or checkpoint-selection bootstrap. They concern prompted quirk confession and do not measure the broad neutral-prompt behavior in the claim. Figure-only per-quirk trajectories and exact per-condition values for trusted-data and inoculation sweeps were also not extracted separately.

untested.parts: All: no insecure-code fine-tuning, no secure or educational controls, no free-form misalignment evaluation.
All: no bad-advice, reward-hack or number-sequence fine-tunes measured for broad misalignment.
All: no in-context induction of broad misalignment.
All: no RL-induced broad misalignment measured.
All: no shared direction or persona analysis of misalignment. The NLA analysis concerns AuditBench quirk verbalization.
Inoculation and benign re-training against emergent misalignment. Inoculation was tested only against subliminal animal-preference transfer (Section 3.4).
All: no effect size, seed or coherence-filter robustness, or training-time emergence of broad misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. They are kept as context for fits_no_version only; their states describe the study's own constructs, not any claim version. The only contact with emergent misalignment is footnote 2 and a related-work sentence that inoculation mitigates emergent misalignment, citing others. Neither yields a rate of misaligned behaviour.

versions.untested_parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning and matched secure-code/class controls; misaligned free-form answers to unrelated neutral prompts.
The listed narrow fine-tuning datasets and broad misaligned answers on unrelated prompts.
Broad misalignment arising from reinforcement learning.
Whether a shared linear direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment across fine-tunes.

Whether inoculation or brief benign re-training prevents or reverses broad misalignment caused by narrow harmful-task fine-tuning. The paper tests inoculation against animal-preference transfer during distillation instead.
Effect size and robustness across seeds and coherence filters, and timing during training for the claimed broad misalignment.
